what_v2_improved: Neutral expression and X mouth change zero authored source pixels.
All 11,376 shared feature pixels have one declared owner.
The worst hard face replacements and ballooned mouth poses from v1 are suppressed.
The exact audio/video clock, single-encoder-process invocation, full frame decode, and delivery stream remain useful infrastructure.

reasons: Gaze and blink transitions show doubled or translucent irises, eyelids, and eye contours.
Mouth states dissolve through the moustache and beard instead of forming physically ordered lips, jaw, cavity, teeth, and tongue.
Several visemes collapse into the same soft smile or dark slit, reducing speech readability.
Attenuating RGB crops traded v1's exaggeration for weak acting without repairing anatomy.
The machine gates validate containment, clock, codec, and sampled encoding fidelity; they do not validate semantic facial topology or artistic quality.

independent_audit_limitations: The atlas states are subtracted from the authored plate rather than from registered neutral/X states, so weighted states remain attenuated atlas replacements rather than true neutral-relative correctives.
The renderer accepts arbitrary output directories, so the recorded single encoder process does not enforce one immutable encode across alternate paths.
The required pre-encode preview is a 16-still sheet and is not bound to the complete 228-frame source, implementation, contract, or an explicit review verdict.
The contract's one-resample claim is false: some feature pixels pass through overlapping cubic shoulder and head warps and then a LANCZOS camera resize.
Decoded eye, mouth, face, and sharpness fidelity was sampled at 16 review frames rather than evaluated on all 228 frames.
Stable identity evidence is pre-warp mask scope, not source-aligned final-frame identity evidence.
Blink and mouth-motion gates are RGB-delta proxies that a brightness flash or wrong repeated blob could satisfy.
Encoded AAC content and audio/visual lag were not decoded and compared to the locked mix.
Mean feature-step gates can hide a localized one-frame pop.
The v2-left/v1-right A/B assignment is fixed and therefore is not genuinely blinded.
A failed render can leak a staging directory if the single rejected-path name already exists.

required_next_representation.first_proof: 60 frames: neutral, bilateral blink, B-to-A-to-F articulation, return to exact neutral, head motion disabled
